transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Orion Head of Infra), Maya (Orion PM), David (Orion Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for making time today, just doing the renewal and expansion check-in, want to make sure we cover capacity, regions and contract length.
[00:14] Carlos: Yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. We got the renewal notice, we're pretty happy with perf, just want to scope out cost if we bump capacity and add eu/apac.
[00:24] Maya: Hi all, also want to make sure the rollout won't impact our peak holiday traffic, that's a hard requirement.
[00:31] Jordan: Totally. Priya is on to go through options; I'll cover commercial.
[00:37] Priya: Hey team, quick note — you mentioned performance is good, can you remind me what your 95th p99 latency targets are for search and personalization calls?
[00:46] Maya: For personalization we need sub 200ms p95 on average and search is okay up to 400ms p95, p99 we'd like under 800 if possible.
[00:56] Priya: Ok that helps. Right now on your dedicated capacity pool we've been seeing median around 120ms for personalization at 8k tokens, p95 about 180 so you're within target. A couple of notes though: when you scale concurrency up we see the KV cache heat-up time change and that can bump p99 for cold start traffic.
[01:15] Carlos: When you say KV cache heat-up can you explain, I'm not super deep on that term.
[01:21] Priya: Sure sorry, KV cache — the key/value cache for transformer decoding. When new shards spin up or if there's a lot of unique prefixes the cache isn't warmed so token generation does extra work, which can add latency spikes. We have cache pre-warming and prefix caching options, also sticky routing to keep sessions on warmed nodes.
[01:38] Carlos: Got it. Could we buy more reserved GPUs to reduce cold starts? Curious about tradeoffs.
[01:43] Jordan: Yes capacity helps. We can offer a committed reserved pool which keeps nodes warm for your allocation — it's more expensive committed spend but lower tail latency. We included two committed tiers in the draft renewal.
[01:54] Maya: And region-wise, we want to add eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. What's the timeline and cost?
[02:01] Priya: For EU we can spin up a dedicated pool in eu-west-1 within 2-3 weeks once we provision capacity from our infra teams, APAC is similar but sometimes a bit longer due to availability; estimate 3-5 weeks. Pricing is per-region reserved capacity plus inter-region data egress if cross-region traffic moves.
[02:18] David: From procurement side, we need to understand the contract change — if we commit to a 12-month extension with tiered capacity what are the termination and true-up clauses?
[02:26] Jordan: We'll propose a 12-month amendment with monthly true-ups and a 60-day notice for downgrades. We can include a minimum commit and have overage rates defined. I'll share a clean amendment for legal.
[02:37] David: Cool. Also can you confirm SOC 2 scope and whether you support our SSO via SAML? We need that for our security review.
[02:44] Jordan: Yes SOC2 Type II available; we also have SAML SSO and SCIM support for provisioning. I'll share the security pack link.
[02:51] Maya: Awesome. On performance tests: we'd like Redwood to run a short benchmark using our production-ish dataset — low latencies at peak QPS matter. Can you scope a 48-hour run in eu-west-1 with dedicated nodes?
[03:02] Priya: Absolutely. We'll do a 48-hour soak with your traffic profile. We'll need the traffic traces and example prompts, and any per-route weights. We'll also run with and without prefix caching and with your proposed batching settings so we can recommend quantization / batch configs.
[03:19] Maya: I'll get that over. Expecting spikes of ~250 RPS for personalization and 120 RPS for search in peak windows.
[03:27] Priya: Good, please include QPS distribution, token lengths, and percentiles. That will let us pick kernel configs and batching.
[03:35] Carlos: On the topic of quantization, we tried a 4-bit model internally and saw regressions in recall for search. Any recommendations?
[03:43] Priya: In our experience 4-bit can work for some models but you have to validate quality. We can recommend mixed profiles — keep personalization on a higher precision profile and quantize search models after evaluation. Redwood Optimize can suggest which layers to keep higher precision.
[03:56] Jordan: Quick commercial note — we've got three pricing options: self-serve hosted, dedicated reserved monthly, and enterprise private (VPC). For your needs the dedicated reserved pool with a 12-month commit looks optimal. We can also include short burst credits for unexpected peaks.
[04:11] David: Would a reserved pool reduce unit cost noticeably? We need numbers to justify procurement.
[04:17] Jordan: Yes. For the volumes you're showing, committed reserved reduces per-token cost by ~22% compared to on-demand dedicated. If you add a 2-region commit there's an additional 6% discount across the committed units. I'll include a worked example.
[04:30] Maya: What about failover — if one region goes down how does traffic shift? We can't have a single point of failure for peak windows.
[04:36] Priya: We support smart routing with automatic failover to a compatible model variant in another region. There will be increased latency due to cross-region hop and possible model variant differences; we recommend canarying and setting fallback policies. Also, prefix caching won't warm across regions, so cold-start penalty applies for failover traffic.
[04:55] Carlos: Ok planning-wise that sounds fine. Security — one more question: do you support customer-managed KMS for key separation?
[05:02] Jordan: Yes we do; for private deployments and some dedicated customers we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS or HSM). We'll note the exact support in the security doc.
[05:10] David: Great. Procurement timeline: if we get the pricing and amendment this week can we sign by mid-May? That's our target.
[05:17] Jordan: We can aim for that. I'll get pricing out by Friday, Priya will share the benchmark plan early next week, and legal will prepare the amendment.
[05:24] Maya: On telemetry — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards. Is that in Redwood Console?
[05:30] Priya: Yes Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, and tracing hooks. We can set up a role for your eng team with read-only access for the trial.
[05:40] Carlos: Speaking of the trial, can we run the benchmark against a small dedicated pool first before committing region-wide?
[05:47] Priya: Yes that's a good approach — a pilot pool in eu-west-1 for the 48-hour test. After validation we can scale.
[05:54] Jordan: I'll include pilot pricing as an addendum — that keeps your procurement footprint smaller to start.
[06:00] David: Legal will need to see liability and data retention language. Do you have standard clauses or do we need to negotiate?
[06:05] Jordan: We have standard enterprise terms. For data retention we can set retention windows and export rights. If you have specifics we can flag them early.
[06:12] Maya: We have a requirement to keep logs for 90 days and audit logs for two years, if that's doable.
[06:18] Priya: That aligns with our enterprise options; we can confirm retention settings and export hooks.
[06:25] Carlos: One operational question — when you say 'sticky routing' is that session level or connection level? We route through a global balancer and can't guarantee sticky connections.
[06:34] Priya: Sticky is session-level — we use a session token to route the request to the warmed node. If your fronting LB strips that token you'll need to pass a header or use persistence at app level. We can document recommended headers.
[06:48] Maya: Ok we might need a small change in our gateway to preserve the session id header. We'll evaluate.
[06:54] Jordan: Great. Any other questions on the product side?
[06:57] David: Not right now. From procurement we'll validate budget numbers once you send the updated pricing.
[07:03] Jordan: Quick recap — I'll send updated pricing with tiered committed options and pilot pricing by Friday. Priya will send benchmark plan and test matrix Monday. Maya will share traffic profiles and token distributions by end of week. Legal will get a draft amendment for a 12-month extension with monthly true-ups. We'll aim to sign mid-May.
[07:22] Maya: Sounds good. Also please include your SOC2 and latest pen test report in the security pack.
[07:28] Jordan: Will do; link to security pack in follow-up.
[07:32] Carlos: Thanks everyone.
[07:34] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and next steps.

(End of transcript — automated transcript contains a few minor mis-hearings and speaker labeling inconsistencies)
notes: Shared artifacts mentioned: pricing deck (link), security pack (SOC2 + pen test) (link), benchmark test plan (to be shared). Transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions (K V cache noted as K V cash in some segments).
